subject: Post-call: Benchmark plan and follow-up (Redwood vs Hyperscaler) - latency & throughput
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@globex.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@globex.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed benchmark plan (Redwood vs Hyperscaler)

Thanks for the call earlier — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you concrete numbers for decisioning:

Summary of Globex goals
- Latency: p95 and p99 targets for single-request inference (token-limited dialogue flows).
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec under steady-state load for concurrent customers.
- Determinism: consistent tail latency across cold vs warm starts.
- Cost guidance: unit cost/tokens at target SLOs.

What Redwood will run (proposed tests)
1) A/B: Redwood hosted inference vs Hyperscaler API (same open model checkpoint)
2) Latency buckets: p50, p95, p99 (ms) — run for batch sizes [1,4,8]
3) Throughput: tokens/sec sustained for target concurrencies (10, 25, 50 workers)
4) Cold-start vs warm-cache runs (3 cold runs, 10 warm runs)
5) Payloads: representative requests you provided and a small randomized sample from your dataset

Deliverables
- CSV with p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec by test matrix
- Logs + artifact bundle (benchmark harness, seed inputs)
- Short executive one-pager with interpretive notes and recommended next tests

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft test plan (globex_test_plan_v1.csv) and the benchmark request PDF.

Next steps
- Please confirm the payloads in the attached CSV (Priya/Alex).
- We’ll run initial A/B tests next week (Rishi will lead execution).
- Schedule 30–45 min sync after we have results (suggest Wed or Thu).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi and Markus to keep execution tight.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

2) KV cache: For multi-turn flows we use KV cache — please run a 6-turn dialogue scenario as part of latency tests.

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Preliminary benchmark results (Redwood vs Hyperscaler) — Feb 24 runs

On Tue, Feb 24, 2026 at 09:08 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Attached is the test plan and payload set. Running A/B in us-west-2.

Quick summary of the initial runs (same payloads, gaia-7b):
- Test matrix: batch sizes = 1, 4, 8; concurrency = 10 workers; 6-turn dialogue for KV cache scenario.
- Redwood (hosted, us-west-2, quantized inference profile):
  - p50: 42 ms (batch=1), 70 ms (b=4), 120 ms (b=8)
  - p95: 120 ms (b=1), 200 ms (b=4), 330 ms (b=8)
  - p99: 210 ms (b=1), 380 ms (b=4), 620 ms (b=8)
  - tokens/sec sustained (concurrency=10): 175 tps
- Hyperscaler API (same model checkpoint, managed endpoint):
  - p50: 55 ms (b=1), 95 ms (b=4), 160 ms (b=8)
  - p95: 180 ms (b=1), 320 ms (b=4), 520 ms (b=8)
  - p99: 320 ms (b=1), 620 ms (b=4), 1150 ms (b=8)
  - tokens/sec sustained: 120 tps

Notes and caveats:
- Cold-starts added ~40–80 ms to p95 on both sides for first request in a new container. Warm-run numbers above.
- We applied batching heuristics and a 10-request lookahead for Redwood to maximize throughput without violating latency SLOs. Hyperscaler runs used their native batching.
- All runs use identical tokenization and the 6-turn KV scenario.

Artifacts attached: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_p95_p99.csv, benchmark_logs.zip. Full run artifacts are in the Drive folder.

Prelim interpretation: Redwood shows consistently better p95/p99 tails and higher sustained tokens/sec for this workload. We should validate under sustained ramp (30 min) and at higher concurrencies (25/50) next.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@globex.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Preliminary benchmark results (Redwood vs Hyperscaler) — Feb 24 runs

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the numbers — helpful. A few follow-ups:

1) Which quantization profile was used on Redwood? Any accuracy/regression numbers vs baseline FP16?
2) Can you share raw request/response sizes (to confirm token accounting)?
3) For sustained throughput, can we run a 30-minute ramp at concurrency=25 and 50? p99 SLO we care about is 300 ms for production traffic.
4) Would you be able to run the same tests from our us-west-2 account with a Redwood-managed cluster in our VPC (private deployment)? We want to verify network egress and interconnect variability.

If you can run the 30-min ramps and share results by EOD Thu, we’ll sync Fri to decide next steps.

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary benchmark results (Redwood vs Hyperscaler) — next steps

Alex — thanks, we can do all of the above. Plan:

1) Quantization & accuracy: Markus will run a brief FP16 vs quant profile check and include top-line accuracy/regression deltas; we’ll attach a short note.
2) Raw sizes: Rishi will include request/response byte counts in the CSV.
3) Sustained ramps: We’ll run two 30-minute sustained ramp tests (concurrency=25 and 50) in us-west-2 tomorrow morning; target: validate p99 < 300 ms at production payload distribution.
4) Private deployment test: Laura will scope a Redwood-managed cluster in your VPC and propose timing/costs (Laura, can you follow up with a short ops checklist?).

Timeline: Rishi will upload ramp artifacts to Drive by EOD Thu (link below). Let’s tentatively schedule a 30 min sync Fri 11:00 PT to review results and next steps.

Action items
- Alex/Priya: confirm that we can run tests against your VPC account (Laura to follow up) and sign the benchmark engagement (simple statement of work) — I’ll send DocuSign.
- Rishi/Markus/Laura: run ramps and accuracy check; upload logs and CSVs.
